findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done.
Case: normal use - A client repo initialized with only Codex later selects Claude as its local cold reader.
Done when: A reviews line in forge.local.toml picks this clone reviewer with the same values as forge.toml, and naming the family that built the item is refused with a message that points to forge.local.toml.
Even after Claude is installed, `story.py:244-246` requires the Claude SDK and `worker.py:483-486` directs the user to `forge doctor --fix` if it is missing. But `doctor.py:574-579` and `sync.py:729-731` do not install that SDK when `tools = "codex"`, so the selected reader remains unusable. The reverse switch from a Claude-only repo to a Codex reader has the same problem with the Codex SDK.
findings.title: Not done: A local cold-reader choice cannot provision the selected SDK

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 3, Harm 3
Raise: Not done.
Case: normal use - Codex commits an initial round, the developer switches the worker to Claude for a later round, then selects Codex as the local reviewer.
Done when: A reviews line in forge.local.toml picks this clone reviewer with the same values as forge.toml, and naming the family that built the item is refused with a message that points to forge.local.toml.
`worker.py:325-327` replaces the recorded worker on each round, and `review.py:840-842` passes only that latest value to this check. Consequently Codex is allowed to review the item even when its earlier changes remain in the reviewed diff; the promised refusal is never shown.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional.
Case: normal use - A teammate updates the approved constitution after this clone last fetched, and a developer then starts a cold read using a local reviewer.
Accepting `reviews` here makes `story.py:166-167` skip the default-branch fetch. The read still obtains the constitution from the last-fetched ref through `story.py:300` and `records.py:635-648`, so it can approve a plan using an obsolete constitution or none at all even though the new one has merged.
Adds work: restore the existing fetch for local-reviewer reads; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 2.
findings.title: Functional: Refresh default-branch rules before a locally configured cold read

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test.
Case: normal use - A repo that was set up for one tool selects the other tool as its local cold reader.
This proof selects only Antigravity, while the shared `repo` fixture installs both Codex and Claude SDKs (`tests/conftest.py:658-669`). It therefore passes while a Codex-only repo cannot provision the locally selected Claude reader, and vice versa: the prescribed `forge doctor --fix` does not install the needed SDK.
findings.title: Test: A local reviews line selects the cold reader

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test.
Case: normal use - An item has work from two builder families after the developer switches workers.
This test supplies one builder directly to `env.start_fix`; that fixture writes the worker field into the internal state (`tests/test_close.py:223-253`) instead of exercising builder rounds. Its assertions still pass even though a later round overwrites the earlier builder and selecting that earlier family is accepted for review.

why: Who reviews or cold reads cannot be switched for one clone without editing the shared forge.toml, which the owner rule of 28 Nov 2026 says must never be needed, for clients too.
